_comment: Server-side register of the numbered normative statements of MQTT 5.0 and MQTT 3.1.1 for mqttiumd. Maintained by hand; see README.md in this directory for the meaning of every field and status. `python3 mqttiumd/conformance/check.py` checks it and rewrites SUMMARY.md.

5.0.note: Every received string passes `Cursor::string`; the test refuses an overlong sequence in a ClientID. Surrogates are refused by the same `from_utf8` call but are not asserted.
A ClientID containing U+0000 is refused as malformed, and a filter containing it is not a valid filter.
A ClientID starting with EF BB BF is kept byte for byte.

A non-minimal Remaining Length is malformed and closes the connection; sent lengths are checked at the 128 and 16,384 boundaries. The same rule for a Property Length (`Cursor::variable`) is not asserted.
Both strings of a User Property are read with `Cursor::string`; no test sends an invalid one.
A PUBREL with flag bits 0000 is malformed, and the first byte of the sent CONNACK, PUBREC and PINGRESP is asserted. The other reserved-flag cases of `flags` are not asserted one by one.
A received QoS 0 PUBLISH decodes without an identifier and the sent one is compared byte for byte.
Binds the client only.
Core level: two outgoing deliveries get identifiers 1 and 2, and an identifier stays unavailable until the finish of its exchange is known.
PUBACK and PUBREC are read from the socket with the identifier of their PUBLISH; PUBCOMP and the broker's own PUBREL are asserted at core level.
The acknowledgement is built from the identifier of the request, but no test compares the identifier of a SUBACK or UNSUBACK with the one sent.
A sent PUBLISH without properties carries a zero Property Length, and a SUBSCRIBE without one is malformed.
Binds the client only. A first packet other than CONNECT closes the connection (`packet_before_connack`).
A second CONNECT closes the connection (event `second_connect`) without a DISCONNECT. No test of the product runtime sends one.
Any other protocol name is malformed: the connection is closed without a CONNACK. Not asserted.

Level 4 is served as MQTT 3.1.1. Any other level gets a 3.1.1-format CONNACK with return code 1 (asserted on the encoder) and the connection is closed; the closing path is asserted with another refusal cause.
A set reserved flag is `ReservedConnectFlag`, malformed, closed without a CONNACK. Not asserted.
Clean Start replaces a stored session by a new one with Session Present 0. The socket-level test exists in the `test-hooks` build only; the store and core tests run in both.
A reconnection with Clean Start 0 gets Session Present 1, keeps its subscription and receives the messages queued while it was away.
An unknown ClientID with Clean Start 0 gets a new session and Session Present 0.
The Will is durable in the store before the CONNECT result is relayed. Only a QoS 1, zero-delay, property-free Will is accepted.

The Will is admitted once after a DISCONNECT whose reason code is not 0x00 (0x04, 0x80 and 0x83 are asserted, and the Will PUBLISH is read on a subscriber's socket), after a take-over and after a restart, and not after DISCONNECT 0x00. A non-zero Will Delay Interval is refused, so that branch does not exist.
A CONNECT with the Will Flag and no Will fields is malformed.
The stored Will is gone after DISCONNECT 0x00 and after its publication.
Will Flag 0 with a non-zero Will QoS is `InvalidWillFlags`.

Only Will QoS 1 is accepted: a CONNECT with Will QoS 0 or 2 is answered with CONNACK 0x83 and closed. Will QoS 3 is a Malformed Packet (`ReservedWillQos`, 0x81 in the event); it supplies no response limit and is closed without a CONNACK.
Will Flag 0 with Will Retain 1 is `InvalidWillFlags`.
The retain bit of the stored Will selects the retained admission; no test asserts that a Will with Will Retain 0 leaves no retained message.
Store level: a Will with Will Retain 1 becomes the retained message of its topic and outlives its source.
Fields are read according to the flags and any byte left over is `TrailingFields`, malformed. Not asserted.
Not offered: a CONNECT with the User Name or Password flag is parsed, then refused with CONNACK 0x83 and closed.
Fields are read according to the flags and any byte left over is `TrailingFields`, malformed. Not asserted.
Not offered: a CONNECT with the User Name or Password flag is parsed, then refused with CONNACK 0x83 and closed.
Binds the client only.
Binds the client only. The broker sends no Server Keep Alive.

With Keep Alive 1, a peer that sent one PINGREQ and then nothing for 1.7 s is closing with the code `keep_alive` at the next check, also while the core has not taken that packet (`keep_alive_expires_a_silent_peer_although_its_last_packet_is_still_held`), and a peer heard every 0.4 s is not closed (`keep_alive_does_not_expire_a_peer_the_broker_keeps_hearing`). Any threshold between 0.4 s and 1.7 s passes both tests: the factor one and a half is read in the code (`keep_alive * 1500` ms since the last complete packet heard, in `connections`), not established by a test. That the closure is handled as a network failure, with the Will published, is not asserted there. Both tests drive MQTT 5 connections. The compatibility scenario `connect/keepalive-timeout-v4` observes a closure within 5 s of silence on a MQTT 3.1.1 socket, not timed. The deadline belongs to the reception of a packet: a packet heard 1.2 s ago and taken by the core only now does not move it.
A session with a finite or infinite interval survives its connection and a graceful stop; one with interval 0 does not.
A refusal larger than the client's limit is not written, and a PUBLISH above it is never emitted. See MQTT-3.1.2-25 for what happens instead.

A QoS 1 or 2 delivery whose PUBLISH would exceed the client's Maximum Packet Size is not sent and ends through the FinishDelivery guarded by its claim; the connection stays open and the next delivery is sent (record 0025 as amended). The core tests cover QoS 1 and 2, with and without Message Expiry, at the exact size and across the Remaining Length step; the runtime test covers QoS 1 on the wire and the resumed session. The test of `tests/packet_limit.rs` drives the product executable over TCP at QoS 1 and QoS 2: nothing is written for the discarded delivery, the event `delivery_discarded` carries `packet_too_large`, the store keeps no obligation and no claim, the next delivery fits the limit, and the session resumed under a larger limit reads a new message first; it is the active successor of the frozen reception F-packet-limit. The compatibility scenarios `publish/over-maximum-packet-size-qos1-v5` and `-qos2-v5` carry the same story as expectations on the transcript, and Mosquitto 2.1.4 answers alike. A QoS 0 copy is dropped (`qos0_fits`). Not covered: a kill of the real process between the claim and its discard (shown on the core with a recovered claim and on both stores with a reopen).
The broker never sends a Topic Alias: `encode_publication` writes no property or the Message Expiry Interval only, and the encoder tests compare whole packets.
The broker never sends a Topic Alias: `encode_publication` writes no property or the Message Expiry Interval only, and the encoder tests compare whole packets.

The CONNACK is a fixed layout without Response Information. A CONNECT with Request Response Information 1 is accepted and gets none, which the statement allows (`information_the_broker_may_leave_unused_does_not_refuse_its_packet`).
The broker never sends a Reason String or a User Property on any packet: every encoder writes a fixed layout. Request Problem Information is parsed and needs no further handling.
Binds the client only.
Binds the client only. The broker reads the fields in that order.
The session found at reconnection, with its subscription and queued messages, is the one of the ClientID.
Binds the client only.
Binds the client only. The broker reads it with `Cursor::string`.

The decoder accepts the identifiers `plain` and `small`, and the runtime opens a session for `first` and for `second` and serves a QoS 2 exchange on them. That is four identifiers of five or six lower-case letters: lengths 1 and 23, digits and upper-case letters are not exercised, and no test sends such a CONNECT on a socket and reads CONNACK 0 (the runtime test checks the type of the CONNACK, not its reason). The tests cited before used identifiers outside the domain of the statement, a hyphen or 1,024 bytes (independent audit of 8e4303d, 21 November 2026). On the mTLS listener the ClientID must also be granted to the certificate.
A zero-length ClientID is not allowed: CONNACK 0x85, then the connection is closed. Nothing is assigned.
A zero-length ClientID is not allowed: CONNACK 0x85, then the connection is closed. No Assigned Client Identifier is ever sent.
An empty ClientID gets CONNACK 0x85 and one above 1,024 bytes CONNACK 0x95, then the connection is closed. The MQTT 5 bytes for these two causes are not asserted.
A non-zero Will Delay Interval is refused with CONNACK 0x83 (`will_profile_refusals_do_not_accept_ignored_properties`), so no delayed Will exists to withhold.
A Will carrying a User Property, or any property other than a zero Will Delay Interval, is refused with CONNACK 0x83.
The Will Topic is read with `Cursor::string` and checked as a Topic Name; ill-formed UTF-8 in it is not asserted.
Not offered: a CONNECT with the User Name or Password flag is parsed, then refused with CONNACK 0x83 and closed.

Codec level: malformed and contradictory CONNECT packets are refused. On the socket, the close of a refused CONNECT that gets no CONNACK is asserted with a well-formed one; no runtime test sends a malformed CONNECT.

On the mTLS listener a ClientID or Will topic not granted to the certificate gets CONNACK 0x87 and the connection is closed. The policy is unit-tested, the refusal path is not; the plaintext listener authenticates nobody.
The previous connection of the ClientID reads DISCONNECT 0x8E and is closed before the new session opens.
Both values of Clean Start are exercised against a stored session.
An accepted CONNECT is answered with CONNACK reason 0x00, on the runtime and on the real executable.
A refused connection is marked closing and its input is no longer read. No test sends data after a refused CONNECT.
With CONNECT and a second packet in one write, nothing is sent before the CONNACK.
A second CONNECT closes the connection before any second CONNACK could be produced. Not asserted.
The acknowledge flags byte is 0 or 1 in every CONNACK the encoder produces.
Clean Start over a stored session answers Session Present 0. The socket-level test exists in the `test-hooks` build only.
Session Present is 1 for a stored session and 0 for an unknown ClientID, read from the socket.
Binds the client only.
Binds the client only.
Every refusing CONNACK has a zero flags byte.
After a refusing CONNACK the connection is gone.
A reason that is not a Connect Reason Code is replaced by 0x83 before it is written.
The condition does not arise: QoS 0, 1 and 2 publications are accepted, and the CONNACK carries no Maximum QoS.
The condition does not arise: QoS 0, 1 and 2 publications are accepted. SUBSCRIBE is granted the QoS it requests.
Binds the client only.
A Will QoS of 0 or 2 is beyond what the broker stores and the CONNECT is refused, with reason 0x83 rather than the recommended 0x9B; the closing path is asserted with another profile refusal.
The condition does not arise: retained messages are supported (Retain Available = 1), including a retained Will.
Binds the client only.

Binds the client only. The CONNACK announces 1,048,584 bytes, the size within which no PUBLISH exceeds the payload limit, and the announcement is a limit: a packet of exactly that size is served and one a byte larger, of any kind, is answered DISCONNECT 0x95 and closed (`a_packet_over_the_announced_maximum_packet_size_is_refused`, and the bench expectation `errors/packet-at-announced-maximum-v5#limit`).
A zero-length ClientID is refused with CONNACK 0x85 and the connection is closed; no identifier is assigned.
Binds the client only. The broker announces Topic Alias Maximum 0.
Binds the client only. A PUBLISH with a Topic Alias is answered with DISCONNECT 0x94.
The broker never sends a Reason String or a User Property on any packet: every encoder writes a fixed layout. Both CONNACK layouts are compared whole.
The broker never sends a Reason String or a User Property on any packet: every encoder writes a fixed layout. Both CONNACK layouts are compared whole.

No Server Keep Alive is sent and the client's value is the one enforced; the enforcement itself is not tested (MQTT-3.1.2-22).
Core level: a delivery replayed after reconnection carries DUP 1, at QoS 1 and 2.
The sent QoS 0 PUBLISH is compared byte for byte, and a received one with DUP is answered with DISCONNECT 0x81 and closed.
The outgoing DUP is `may_have_started` of the delivery and the incoming DUP is not stored; no test varies the incoming flag and observes the outgoing one.
QoS 3 is `InvalidQos` in the header parser: the connection is answered with DISCONNECT 0x81 and closed. The test of that answer sends the DUP flag at QoS 0, not QoS 3.
Store and core level: a retained publication is stored without subscribers and replaces the previous one.
Store level: an empty retained publication removes the stored value and is still published live.
Store level: after the empty publication the retained table is empty.
Only a PUBLISH with RETAIN 1 produces the retained recipe; no test asserts that a non-retained publication leaves an existing retained message in place.
Store level: a subscription with Retain Handling 0 is owed every matching retained message.
Store level: with Retain Handling 1 a new subscription is replayed and a repeated one is not.
Store level, asserted through one filter subscribed three times (Retain Handling 2, 1, 0): only the last adds replays.
Component level: routing computes the per-destination flag and the store keeps it per delivery. No test reads the RETAIN bit of a forwarded PUBLISH on a socket.
Component level: routing computes the per-destination flag and the store keeps it per delivery. No test reads the RETAIN bit of a forwarded PUBLISH on a socket.
The Topic Name is the first field decoded and the first field written.
A PUBLISH to `a/+` is a Protocol Error (reason 0x90).
A destination is selected only when its filter matches the published Topic Name, which is forwarded unchanged; the forwarded name is not compared on a socket.
Payload Format Indicator (0x01) is validated (UTF-8 enforced when 1) and forwarded unaltered to MQTT 5 subscribers across QoS 0/1/2 and retained restarts (ADR 0053).
An expired copy is disposed before its first byte, on the write path and in the store.
The writer replaces the interval by the remaining lifetime at the first byte it sends.

Binds the client only.
The broker never sends a Topic Alias: `encode_publication` writes no property or the Message Expiry Interval only, and the encoder tests compare whole packets.
Not offered: the CONNACK announces Topic Alias Maximum 0, so there is no value to accept; a PUBLISH with a Topic Alias is answered with DISCONNECT 0x94.
Response Topic (0x08) must be a valid MQTT UTF-8 Encoded String; malformed UTF-8 is rejected with DISCONNECT 0x81 and valid values are forwarded unaltered (ADR 0053).
Response Topic containing '+' or '#' is rejected as a Protocol Error (0x82) and never forwarded (ADR 0053).
Response Topic (0x08) is forwarded unaltered on MQTT 5 deliveries and stripped for MQTT 3.1.1 (ADR 0053).
Correlation Data (0x09) binary bytes are forwarded unaltered on MQTT 5 deliveries and stripped for MQTT 3.1.1 (ADR 0053).
All User Properties (0x26) are forwarded unaltered to MQTT 5 subscribers across QoS 0/1/2 and retained restarts, and stripped for MQTT 3.1.1 (ADR 0053).
User Properties (0x26) preserve exact insertion order, including duplicate keys, across QoS 0/1/2 and retained restarts (ADR 0053).
Content Type (0x03) must be a valid MQTT UTF-8 Encoded String; malformed UTF-8 is rejected with DISCONNECT 0x81 and valid values are forwarded unaltered (ADR 0053).
Content Type (0x03) and all other PUBLISH application properties survive retained storage and broker restarts (ADR 0053).
QoS 1 is answered with PUBACK and QoS 2 with PUBREC on the socket; QoS 0 produces no acknowledgement.
Core level: overlapping subscriptions of one session give one delivery at their maximum QoS.
Not offered: CONNACK announces Subscription Identifiers Available = 0, and a SUBSCRIBE that carries one is answered with DISCONNECT 0xA1 and closed (0x83 before 81acd13).
Not offered: CONNACK announces Subscription Identifiers Available = 0, and a SUBSCRIBE that carries one is answered with DISCONNECT 0xA1 and closed (0x83 before 81acd13).
Not offered: CONNACK announces Subscription Identifiers Available = 0, and a SUBSCRIBE that carries one is answered with DISCONNECT 0xA1 and closed (0x83 before 81acd13).

Binds the client only. The broker announces Receive Maximum 8 and answers a ninth open exchange with DISCONNECT 0x93.
Binds the client only.
With Receive Maximum 8, eight of twelve queued messages are written and the rest follow the PUBACKs.
Core level: with a full window of one, the PUBREL of another exchange is still emitted. No socket-level test holds a full window and reads another packet type on the same connection.
PUBACK is written with 0x00, 0x10 (accepted without a matching subscription, record 0049), 0x97 or 0x83 only; the type cannot hold another reason.
The broker never sends a Reason String or a User Property on any packet: every encoder writes a fixed layout. The PUBACK layouts are compared whole.
The broker never sends a Reason String or a User Property on any packet: every encoder writes a fixed layout. The PUBACK layouts are compared whole.

The encoder refuses a PUBREC with 0x92; 0x00, 0x97 and 0x83 are the only others it can write. A PUBREC that accepts is always 0x00, also for a publication without a matching subscription (record 0049).
The broker never sends a Reason String or a User Property on any packet: every encoder writes a fixed layout. Only the successful PUBREC layout is compared whole.
The broker never sends a Reason String or a User Property on any packet: every encoder writes a fixed layout. Only the successful PUBREC layout is compared whole.
A PUBREL with flag bits 0000 is malformed; the reader closes the connection on a header error.
The broker's PUBREL is always the two-byte form, reason 0x00 implied; its bytes are not asserted.
The broker never sends a Reason String or a User Property on any packet: every encoder writes a fixed layout. The PUBREL bytes are not asserted.
The broker never sends a Reason String or a User Property on any packet: every encoder writes a fixed layout. The PUBREL bytes are not asserted.
The encoder refuses a PUBCOMP with a reason other than 0x00 and 0x92.
The broker never sends a Reason String or a User Property on any packet: every encoder writes a fixed layout. The MQTT 5 PUBCOMP bytes are not asserted.
The broker never sends a Reason String or a User Property on any packet: every encoder writes a fixed layout. The MQTT 5 PUBCOMP bytes are not asserted.
Flag bits other than 0010 are `InvalidFixedFlags`: the connection is answered with DISCONNECT 0x81 and closed. Not asserted for SUBSCRIBE.
Each filter is read with `Cursor::string`; ill-formed UTF-8 in a filter is not asserted.
A SUBSCRIBE without a filter is `EmptySubscriptionList`, a Protocol Error. Not asserted.
Core and store level: a No Local subscription gets neither the live nor the retained message of its own ClientID.
No Local on a `$share/` filter is `InvalidSubscriptionOptions`, a Protocol Error. Not asserted.

The independent audit of 8e4303d, 21 November 2026, observed DISCONNECT 0x82 (Protocol Error) for reserved option bits. Since 81acd13 the decoder treats them as a Malformed Packet: the test requires the kind Malformed and the reason 0x81 for the bits 0x40, 0x80 and 0xC0 of a MQTT 5 SUBSCRIBE. That the connection is then closed after DISCONNECT 0x81 is not asserted by a Rust test; the compatibility scenario `subscribe/reserved-option-bits-v5` observes it on a socket.

A SUBSCRIBE is answered with a SUBACK, after its durable commit. A request with more than eight filters is served as unit requests and answered once; a filter longer than the profile stores is refused in the SUBACK (0x97) and its neighbours are granted.
The SUBACK is built from the identifier of the SUBSCRIBE; no test compares the two.
Core level: subscribing again to the same filter leaves one route with the last QoS and options.
A repeated filter with Retain Handling 0 is replayed (store level), and a delivery already owed survives the replacement (core level).

Several filters in one SUBSCRIBE are applied in order and answered by one SUBACK. A request with more filters than the core takes in one request is served as its unit requests, in order, and acknowledged once; the packet is the only bound. On real sockets, in both protocol versions: twelve filters are granted and a message on the twelfth is delivered; nine are removed and a message on the ninth is no longer delivered while one on a kept filter is. The compatibility bench holds the same as absolute expectations.
One reason code per filter, asserted at core level and on the encoder.
The reason is the granted QoS, which is the requested one, or a failure such as 0x97.
Core and store level: a live or retained delivery has the minimum of the published and granted QoS.
The broker never sends a Reason String or a User Property on any packet: every encoder writes a fixed layout. The SUBACK layout is compared whole.
The broker never sends a Reason String or a User Property on any packet: every encoder writes a fixed layout. The SUBACK layout is compared whole.
Core level: the results [2, 0] follow the order of the two filters.

The broker produces a granted QoS, 0x87, 0x8F or 0x97; the QoS and 0x97 results are asserted, the other two are not. The core's 0x9E for a `$share/` filter no longer reaches a MQTT 5 SUBACK since 81acd13: such a SUBSCRIBE is a Protocol Error.
Flag bits other than 0010 are `InvalidFixedFlags`: the connection is answered with DISCONNECT 0x81 and closed. Not asserted for UNSUBSCRIBE.
Each filter is read with `Cursor::string`; ill-formed UTF-8 in a filter is not asserted.
An UNSUBSCRIBE without a filter is `EmptySubscriptionList`, a Protocol Error. Not asserted.
Core level: UNSUBSCRIBE `a/+` leaves the subscription `a/#` and answers 0x11; the exact filter removes it.
Core level: the route is removed when the UNSUBACK is produced. No test publishes afterwards and observes that nothing is delivered.
Core level: a delivery admitted before the UNSUBSCRIBE is still claimed and sent.
Core level: each UNSUBSCRIBE produces an UNSUBACK. On a socket, an UNSUBSCRIBE of nine filters and one of sixty-five are each answered with one UNSUBACK that carries a code per filter.
Core level: an UNSUBSCRIBE that removes nothing is answered with 0x11. The identifier of the UNSUBACK is not compared with the request.

A request with more filters than the core takes in one request is served as its unit requests, in order, and acknowledged once; the packet is the only bound. On real sockets, in both protocol versions: twelve filters are granted and a message on the twelfth is delivered; nine are removed and a message on the ninth is no longer delivered while one on a kept filter is. The compatibility bench holds the same as absolute expectations.
The broker never sends a Reason String or a User Property on any packet: every encoder writes a fixed layout. The MQTT 5 UNSUBACK bytes are not asserted.
The broker never sends a Reason String or a User Property on any packet: every encoder writes a fixed layout. The MQTT 5 UNSUBACK bytes are not asserted.
One code is appended per filter in packet order; no test sends several filters.
The encoder refuses a code that is not an Unsubscribe Reason Code; 0x00 and 0x11 are asserted at core level.
A PINGREQ written to the socket is answered with PINGRESP.
A refusal of a packet pipelined behind CONNECT waits: the client reads CONNACK 0x00, then DISCONNECT.

Non-zero flag bits are `InvalidFixedFlags`, a Malformed Packet: the client reads DISCONNECT 0x81 and the connection is closed, asserted on the executable for a DISCONNECT with reserved bits and eight other packet types.
A reason that is not a Disconnect Reason Code is replaced by 0x83 before it is written; a received server-only reason is a Protocol Error.
The broker's DISCONNECT is a fixed four-byte layout with a zero Property Length.
The broker never sends a Reason String or a User Property on any packet: every encoder writes a fixed layout. The DISCONNECT layout is compared whole.
The broker never sends a Reason String or a User Property on any packet: every encoder writes a fixed layout. The DISCONNECT layout is compared whole.

An attached session is not expired although its interval has passed on the clock.
A detached session is removed from the store at its deadline, and at once when the interval is 0, whether the CONNECT or a DISCONNECT of any legal reason code set it.
TCP, and TLS 1.3 over TCP on the secure listener. Framing is independent of segment boundaries.
The sent QoS 0 PUBLISH is compared byte for byte: QoS 0, DUP 0.
Core level: each new delivery draws an identifier that no unfinished claim holds.
Core level: the first emission of a QoS 1 delivery has DUP 0.
A delivery stays owed until its PUBACK is committed: it is replayed after a reconnection and holds its window slot.
The PUBACK carries the identifier of the PUBLISH and is emitted only after the durable admission.
A PUBLISH reusing an acknowledged identifier, DUP set or not, is a new admission.
Core level: the identifier of a QoS 2 delivery stays reserved until PUBCOMP is committed.
DUP is `may_have_started` for both QoS; the first emission is asserted with DUP 0 for QoS 1 only.
Core level: the PUBLISH holds its window slot until the PUBREC is committed.
Core level: PUBREL with the same identifier follows the committed PUBREC.
Core level: the exchange stays open until PUBCOMP and its PUBREL is replayed after recovery.
Core level: a recovered exchange awaiting PUBCOMP replays PUBREL, not PUBLISH.

A delivery whose PUBLISH is known to have started, or that awaits PUBCOMP, is sent again whatever its lifetime (`expiry_allows_send`), and the writer gives a started frame a remaining interval of 0 instead of withholding it (`prepare_expiry`). No test exercises this for an outgoing QoS 2 delivery, the sender the statement is about: `a_known_started_exchange_replays_with_zero_after_expiry_or_clock_uncertainty` writes a QoS 0 frame (`encode_qos0_expiring`) and `message_expiry_started_claim_replays_past_ttl_and_old_facts_cannot_hit_reused_pi` replays a QoS 1 delivery (independent audit of 8e4303d, 21 November 2026); no test with an outgoing QoS 2 delivery that carries an expiry was found.
PUBREC with the identifier of the PUBLISH is emitted after the durable admission.
After a refusing PUBREC the identifier is free and its receive credit returned.
A repeated PUBLISH is answered with PUBREC again and creates no second admission, also across a reconnection.
PUBCOMP with the identifier of the PUBREL is emitted after the durable release.
A PUBLISH reusing the identifier after PUBCOMP is a new exchange.
An expired inbound QoS 2 message keeps its exchange until PUBREL and PUBCOMP.
Core level: unacknowledged PUBLISH and PUBREL are replayed with their identifiers after a reconnection, and never on a live connection.
Core level: a PUBACK with 0x80 finishes the delivery. The same rule for a refusing PUBREC (`after_pubrec`) is not asserted.
A QoS 1 publication is stored for the matching offline session before its PUBACK and delivered at reconnection.

With the committed result of a first admission kept unknown to the core by a test barrier, a second publication of the same client is admitted and acknowledged, and the subscriber still reads the first then the second: asserted on real sockets for both protocol versions at QoS 1 and 2 (instrumented build). Partial: one publisher and one subscriber, two messages; the order at a takeover, across a crash inside a group commit and when the write itself is late is not asserted. A session that was offline reads twelve messages in order across the two pages its window cuts them into, in both versions at QoS 1 and 2 (`a_resumed_session_reads_its_backlog_in_the_order_of_reception`). The compatibility scenario `publish/burst-qos0-v4` compares the order of the QoS 0 messages of a burst.
Every topic takes one path and there is no unordered mode. That the path keeps the order of reception is the evidence of MQTT-4.6.0-5, with its limits.
A Topic Name containing a wildcard is refused.

An empty Will Topic is refused as Topic Name Invalid (0x90). An empty PUBLISH topic designates nothing without a Topic Alias, and none is accepted: it is a Protocol Error (0x82), asserted on the wire. An empty filter is refused by `codec::filter` (not asserted) and by the core's grammar (asserted).
U+0000 is refused in every string and in the core's filter grammar.
The broker's own bound is 1,024 bytes: a longer Topic Name or filter is refused (DISCONNECT 0x95).
Matching is byte-exact: `a` does not match `A`, nor `é/#` the topic `e/x`.

With Keep Alive 1, a peer that sent one PINGREQ and then nothing for 1.7 s is closing with the code `keep_alive` at the next check, also while the core has not taken that packet (`keep_alive_expires_a_silent_peer_although_its_last_packet_is_still_held`), and a peer heard every 0.4 s is not closed (`keep_alive_does_not_expire_a_peer_the_broker_keeps_hearing`). Any threshold between 0.4 s and 1.7 s passes both tests: the factor one and a half is read in the code (`keep_alive * 1500` ms since the last complete packet heard, in `connections`), not established by a test. That the closure is handled as a network failure, with the Will published, is not asserted there. Both tests drive MQTT 5 connections; the check has no branch on the protocol version. The compatibility scenario `connect/keepalive-timeout-v4` observes a closure within 5 s of silence on a MQTT 3.1.1 socket, not timed. The deadline belongs to the reception of a packet: a packet heard 1.2 s ago and taken by the core only now does not move it.

Written for the Client; MQTT-4.6.0-6 extends 'the rules listed above' to a Server. Record 0050 keeps the order whatever the reading: the core holds a PUBACK that would overtake the answer of an earlier publication of the same connection and releases it in its turn. Asserted in the core with the results of two admissions applied in reverse order, and with a chain of three released by the receipts; on real sockets, with the committed result of the first admission kept unknown by a test barrier and then resolved by the SQLite store, no acknowledgement leaves before that of the first publication, in both protocol versions (instrumented build). The independent audit of 8e4303d, 21 November 2026, had observed 8 then 7 for publications received as 7 then 8. Partial: the order is that of one connection; across a takeover by another connection each has its own, and the oracle has no assertion on it.

Asserted in the core with the results of two admissions applied in reverse order, and with a chain of three released by the receipts; on real sockets, with the committed result of the first admission kept unknown by a test barrier and then resolved by the SQLite store, no acknowledgement leaves before that of the first publication, in both protocol versions (instrumented build); on the bench, scenario ORDER-A through the real core on both stores. The independent audit of 8e4303d, 21 November 2026, had observed 8 then 7 for publications received as 7 then 8. Partial: the order is that of one connection; across a takeover by another connection each has its own, and the oracle has no assertion on it.

Written for the Client; MQTT-4.6.0-6 extends 'the rules listed above' to a Server for its deliveries. The core sends the PUBREL of a delivery only when no PUBREL of an earlier PUBREC of the same session is still being prepared: asserted in the core with two preparations answered by the store in reverse order (the probe of the independent audit, which showed 2 then 1 before the correction). On real sockets, with the committed result of the first preparation kept unknown by a test barrier and then resolved by the SQLite store, no PUBREL leaves while the earlier one is unknown and the two leave in the order of the PUBRECs, in both versions (instrumented build; the test fails on the core before the correction). A resumed session that answers a backlog of twelve QoS 2 deliveries receives its PUBRELs in the order of its PUBRECs. Partial: two deliveries of one session under the barrier; not asserted at a takeover nor across a crash between two preparations.
Every topic takes one path and there is no unordered mode. That the path keeps the order of reception is the evidence described under MQTT-4.6.0-6, with its limits.

Both requirements have a witness, each partial. The order of deliveries: with the committed result of a first admission kept unknown to the core by a test barrier, a second publication of the same client is admitted and acknowledged, and the subscriber still reads the first then the second: asserted on real sockets for both protocol versions at QoS 1 and 2 (instrumented build). Partial: one publisher and one subscriber, two messages; the order at a takeover, across a crash inside a group commit and when the write itself is late is not asserted. A session that was offline reads twelve messages in order across the two pages its window cuts them into, in both versions at QoS 1 and 2 (`a_resumed_session_reads_its_backlog_in_the_order_of_reception`). The compatibility scenario `publish/burst-qos0-v4` compares the order of the QoS 0 messages of a burst. The other requirement, 'the rules listed above when delivering messages to each of its subscribers', covers the order of PUBREL after PUBREC on a delivery: see MQTT-4.6.0-4.
